title: Infrastructure as code
summary: How cloud resources are created and changed, so that every environment can be rebuilt and every change is reviewed.
scope: Everything created in GCP or Azure for an application. Sandboxes for experiments are out of scope.

requirements.title: No manual changes
requirements.statement: Resources in test, staging and production are created and changed only through Terraform in a pipeline, never by hand in a console.
requirements.rationale: A manual change cannot be reviewed, is lost on the next apply, and makes environments drift apart.
guidance: Make the change in the Terraform code and open a pull request.
For an emergency fix in a console, raise a follow-up to bring the code in line within one working day.

verification.description: Drift detection runs nightly and reports differences to the owning team.

requirements.title: Use the platform modules
requirements.statement: Resources are created with the modules from the platform catalogue where one exists.
requirements.rationale: The modules already apply naming, labels, encryption and network rules.
guidance: Search the module catalogue before writing a raw resource.
If no module fits, ask in #cloud-platform before writing your own.

lookFor: A raw google_* or azurerm_* resource for which a platform module exists (bucket, database, service account, network)

requirements.title: Pin versions
requirements.statement: Providers and modules are pinned to an exact version or tag.
requirements.rationale: An unpinned version changes what an apply does without any change in your code.

verification.description: Lint rule in the Terraform pipeline.

lookFor: A provider version constraint using >=, ~> or no version at all

requirements.title: Labels on every resource
requirements.statement: Every resource carries the labels application-id, environment and cost-centre.
requirements.rationale: Cost and ownership reports are built from these labels.

lookFor: A resource or module block without labels or tags

requirements.title: Remote, locked state
requirements.statement: Terraform state is stored in the platform's remote backend with locking. State files are never committed.
requirements.rationale: State holds secrets and is the only record of what Terraform manages. A lost or conflicting state breaks every later change.
guidance: Use the backend block from the platform template.

lookFor: No backend block at all in a root module
